license_note: The downloadable weights carry the custom Qwen3.8-Max License, which grants use, modification, distribution, hosting, and fine-tuning but requires attribution above 100 million monthly active users or 20 million US dollars in monthly revenue and a separate license for model-as-a-service or AI-work-assistant businesses above 50 million US dollars in trailing revenue. Hosted qwen3.8-max API use is governed separately by QwenCloud and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio service terms, not by the weights license.

license_evidence.scope: Model weights, parameters, configuration files, inference code, and associated documentation in the Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Hugging Face repository; does not cover the hosted qwen3.8-max API service

access_boundary: This record represents the qwen3.8-max API release of August 3, 2026 together with its open-weights checkpoint Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and the official FP8 sibling. The downloaded checkpoint is narrower than the API namesake (text-only, thinking-required, 262K native context versus the API's vision input and 1M default context). The qwen3.8-max-0902 upgraded snapshot, the qwen3.8-max-preview API preview, the Apache-2.0 Qwen3.8-27B sibling, earlier Qwen generations, QwenCloud product packaging, and community quantizations remain separate boundaries.
strengths: The first Max-class Qwen with downloadable weights (2.4T total, 95B active MoE) plus documented vLLM, SGLang, and TokenSpeed recipes and an official FP8 variant
First-party QwenCloud and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio serving with 1M context plus a documented NVIDIA NIM third-party path for the exact checkpoint
tradeoffs: The custom weights license gates commercial model-as-a-service use above a revenue threshold behind a separate license, unlike earlier Apache-2.0 Qwen generations
The 4.89 TB BF16 checkpoint needs multi-node serving, putting self-operation out of reach for most operators
